title: Class, survey, structure and statutory certification - existing-answer enrichment
note: Enrichment batch: every action edits an EXISTING canonical card. No card is created, removed, renamed or re-anchored. Canonical total is unchanged at 721. Every edit is purely additive - proven by character-level diff opcodes carrying insert operations only, zero delete and zero replace.
followup_overlap: two of ten targets appear in the consolidation's 9 followup_colocation records: QB1_E.html#q1 (GAP-0172, GAP-0282) and QB3_H.html#q6 (GAP-0385). In both cases the follow-up ask is a DIFFERENT limb from the authorised enrichment, so neither was implemented here; both remain open follow-up work.
sibling_pin_delegation: No earlier manifest pins any of the ten E2 targets - checked against batch_a/b/c/d, batch_e_gap0609, batch_e3 and batch_e4 manifests. E2 therefore needs no digest-pin exemption of its own.

cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks the class-status ladder - suspension against withdrawal, what triggers each, whether it is automatic, and the consequence chain to statutory certificates, insurance cover and trading.
changed_sections: answer-body: new h4 '4. Class Status Ladder - Suspension Against Withdrawal' + lead paragraph + one 4-item list + consequence paragraph + closing note
reg-box: two new reg-items (IACS PR 1C Rev.7; Institute Time Clauses - Hulls 1/11/95 cl.4 and 5.1)
authority: IACS Procedural Requirement PR 1C, "Procedure for Suspension and Reinstatement or Withdrawal of Class in Case of Surveys or Conditions of Class Going Overdue", Rev.7 Nov 2024, applying from 1 January 2026 - extracted verbatim from the IACS PDF: A.1.1 (Special Survey, automatic), A.1.2/A.1.3 (Annual/Intermediate, automatic at 3 months), A.2.1 (conditions of class, suspension PROCEDURE), A.4.1 (withdrawal after 6 months), B.1.3 (statutory certificates implicitly invalidated), Definitions ("Disclassed")

Institute Time Clauses - Hulls 1/11/95, clause 4.1.1/4.1.2 (duty to maintain class and comply by the Society’s dates), 4.3 (prompt reporting of any incident, condition or damage), and clause 5.1 (automatic termination on change, suspension, discontinuance, withdrawal or expiry of class, deferred until next port if at sea) - extracted verbatim
cards.authorisation_correction: The consolidation listed "unreported casualty" among the triggers of class suspension. PR 1C does not carry it: the instrument is expressly confined to surveys and conditions of class going overdue, and lists no casualty-reporting ground. The verified duty to report promptly is an ITC-Hulls clause 4.3 obligation, so it was written as a reporting duty whose breach bites through the insurance conditions, NOT as a PR 1C suspension trigger.

cards.missing_limb: The Hull survey card covers survey types, close-up scope and UTM but never names or grades a deformation defect, and never states what turns one into a Condition of Class.
cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks the deformation vocabulary a surveyor actually uses, how it is assessed, and what makes a deformation a Condition of Class.
changed_sections: answer-body: new h4 '4. Reading a Hull Deformation - the Vocabulary a Surveyor Uses' + lead paragraph + one 5-item list + assessment paragraph
reg-box: one new reg-item (IACS Rec. No. 84 Rev.1)
authority: IACS Recommendation No. 84, "Container Ships - Guidelines for Surveys, Assessment and Repair of Hull Structures", Rev.1 Nov 2017, downloaded from the IACS public store and text-extracted: 3.3.4 (deformation from in-plane/out-of-plane/combined loads; local vs global; buckling defined as a small in-plane load increase producing large deformation; permanent vs elastic buckling and how elastic buckling is detected; buckling in webs of web frames and floors; impact/contact and inadvertent overloading; slamming forward and pooping aft), 5.x.2.2 (plate buckling between stiffeners; cross-deck strips; cargo-handling and green-seas deformation), 3.4.2 (any damage considered to affect classification is to be repaired), 3.4.4 (crop and renew at permissible minimum thickness; doubler plates must not compensate wasted plate), 3.4.5 (net scantling approach, UR S11A and S21A, renewal thickness)
cards.authorisation_correction: The consolidation named the vocabulary as "buckling, set-in/dishing of plating, tripping of stiffeners and permanent set". Only buckling is IACS vocabulary here: the strings "tripping", "set-in", "dishing" and "permanent set" each occur ZERO times in IACS Rec. No. 84, the governing guideline for this ship type. The limb was therefore implemented with the taxonomy IACS actually uses (local vs global deformation; buckling; permanent vs elastic buckling) and the four unverified terms were dropped rather than presented to a candidate as class vocabulary.
claims_added: doubler plates must not be used

cards.missing_limb: The answer body opens "a mandatory survey regime under SOLAS" without naming the chapter, and the term "ESP Code" occurs zero times anywhere on the card - the Code is never named as an instrument, only its adopting resolution number appears.
cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks the chapter in the defining prose and the Code by name - it cites A.1049(27) but never says "SOLAS XI-1/2" in the body or "2011 ESP Code" at all.
changed_sections: answer-body: one new paragraph 'The citation, stated precisely' inside the existing 'What ESP Is' section
authority: SOLAS consolidated edition 2024, chapter XI-1 regulation 2 (Enhanced surveys), quoted from the local official-sources copy: bulk carriers as defined in regulation IX/1.6 and oil tankers as defined in regulation II-1/2.22 shall be subject to an enhanced programme of inspections in accordance with the International Code on the Enhanced Programme of Inspections during Surveys of Bulk Carriers and Oil Tankers, 2011 (2011 ESP Code), adopted by the Assembly by resolution A.1049(27); and regulation XI-1/2-1 for cargo ships not subject to the ESP Code
IMO Assembly resolution A.1049(27) - local True Source copy of the 2011 ESP Code held and text-extractable
cards.authorisation_correction: The consolidation asserted that the regulatory citation "is the one part of this four-part ask the card does not answer". cards.q_text: State the Damage Stability Criteria for cargo ships under SOLAS 2009 amendments. What is A ≥ R?
cards.missing_limb: The card states the margin line position (76 mm below the bulkhead deck at side), that the damaged waterline could not submerge it, and that the 2009 amendments deleted it - but never why it sat there.
cards.limb_sentence: The current answer lacks the reason the margin line sat 76 mm below the bulkhead deck at side, so the candidate can explain the principle rather than only report the deletion.
changed_sections: answer-body: one new paragraph 'Why it sat where it did' inside the existing Margin Line section
authority: Technical reasoning only, as the family record specifies. Verified against the local SOLAS consolidated edition 2024: the string "margin line" occurs ZERO times in the current consolidated text, confirming the card’s existing statement that the 2009 amendments removed the concept. The rationale given is the standard subdivision principle - the bulkhead deck is the deck to which transverse watertight bulkheads are carried, so immersion at side permits flow over the bulkhead tops (progressive flooding) and loss of the horizontal escape route - with 76 mm being the original three-inch imperial reserve.
cards.scope_note_honoured: The family record’s bloat_caution required one or two sentences inside the existing Margin Line section rather than a new section, because this is the largest target in the set. Honoured - a single paragraph was added in place, and no new section was created.
